methods: Independent source inspection of actual Sites Worker packager, CI workflows, Supabase worker/scheduler/ledger and release/recovery procedures.
Read-only Node verification of237 manifest source/artifact/migration entries: zero mismatches; enumerated missing guest-support migration.
Read-only public HEAD checks: /200, /check200, /health404; sanitized root live-service baseline for active function versions and aggregate budget.
No suites rerun, build/deployment changes, secret retrieval, paid requests or private candidate reads.
not_tested: Live deployed edge-function source bytes/import graph or schema migration-history digests; active version metadata cannot prove parity.
Authenticated end-to-end workflow, provider calls, production concurrency, failover, backup contents, actual restore or rollout rehearsal.
GitHub workflow executions/branch protections, provider invoices, undocumented external alerting or backup configuration.

criteria.name: Build reproducibility and deployment safety
criteria.evidence: npm lockfile, public-only config, npm ci and Node22 CI plus deterministic Worker checks; auxiliary Pages path ignores failures and chooses public after dist.

criteria.name: Release traceability and layer compatibility
criteria.evidence: 237 manifest entries verify locally; rollback tag/Sites version and backend compatibility documented, but guest-support migration omitted and deployed bytes unverified.

criteria.name: Reliability and recovery readiness
criteria.evidence: Leases, checkpoints, additive migrations and safe rollback exist; data restore remains unrehearsed and recovery objectives expressly unestablished.

criteria.name: Operational health and diagnostics
criteria.evidence: Private operations and Cron/log procedures exist; ready measures attempted dispatch and errors lack correlation; generic operations guide is stale.

criteria.name: Cost and pilot guardrails
criteria.evidence: SQL row-locked50m-micro ceiling, ten seats, conservative reservations and retained uncertain spend; root aggregate baseline reports$0.740100 committed. External/provider charges still require reconciliation.

strengths: Actual production architecture is appropriately small: Sites-hosted Cloudflare Worker plus existing Supabase; no VM/container platform is needed.
Worker package enforces identity, compressed-size bound, private-path denial, canonical redirects, cache policy and security headers; CI checks responses.
Local backend source/artifact hashes are consistent, and saved frontend/backend rollback constraints preserve candidate data and spend ledger.
Database-enforced shared cap and uncertain-call reservation retention are credible guardrails; payments remain disabled.

findings.problem: The edge bundle manifest omits the new guest-support migration; it cannot describe the complete database contract of the functions it packages.

evidence.detail: Migration inclusion matches only _job_loop_ or _jobvance_admin_. Guest-support is in loopNames at line6, but 20261014020000_jobvance_guest_support.sql is absent from manifest.migrations.
Read-only hash verification checked237 source/artifact/migration entries with zero mismatches; completeness is the defect, not stale checked hashes.

findings.recommendation: Include all active-feature migrations through an explicit reviewed allowlist or dependency inventory. Make CI reject missing dependency migrations and emit a release receipt joining Sites version/source SHA, edge artifact hash/version, schema migration hashes and rollback compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Guest-support migration appears with its normalized digest; all currently recorded digests still match.
A fixture omitting a required migration fails validation.
Receipt identifies v19/runtime57713fb and exact backend contracts without retrieving secret values.
findings.cost_effect: No additional service subscription; prevents manual release reconciliation.

findings.problem: Scheduler readiness proves a recent dispatch attempt, not successful worker acceptance or useful progress; downstream failures can leave the ready flag true.

evidence.detail: last_dispatch_at is updated before net.http_post at line27; ready at lines36–38 checks enabled/origin/Cron/recent timestamp and does not inspect HTTP response or completion.
Background scheduler/stage catches log error.name only; stage catch at line23 lacks a run correlation reference.
Operator monitoring relies on manually inspecting Cron and function logs.

findings.recommendation: Show attempted dispatch separately from worker acknowledgement and last successful progress. Surface overdue due jobs and stale active runs in the existing private operations portal, using redacted correlation references and a documented daily check during this pilot.
acceptance_criteria: A mocked worker500 or timeout increments an actionable failure/overdue state despite Cron continuing.
A successful due dispatch records acknowledgement and phase progress; idle queues remain healthy.
Diagnostics include event code and run/dispatch reference without candidate text, tokens or email.
findings.cost_effect: Uses existing database/portal; bounded retention avoids unneeded logging cost.

findings.problem: A frontend rollback is documented, but recoverability of private database records and cloud artifacts remains unproven before widening the pilot.

evidence.detail: Exact saved Sites version14, Git tag and backend rollback constraints are preserved; these restore code, not deleted/corrupted candidate data.
RPO24h/RTO8h are explicitly future objectives contingent on funded backups and a restore rehearsal.
No backup/restore SLA is established; restoration is to be tested separately.

findings.recommendation: Define an owner-operated encrypted backup and restore procedure covering Postgres ownership/policies, required storage objects and artifact metadata, with a deletion/retention rule. Rehearse on isolated synthetic data before enrolling more candidates; choose a funded option only if the owner later accepts its separate cost.
acceptance_criteria: An isolated rehearsal restores a synthetic approved packet and its matching files, ownership isolation and usage ledger.
Record actual restore time/data-loss window and responsible operator; do not promise the unachieved objectives.
Demonstrate that restored approval/erasure semantics remain correct and backup retention is documented.
dependencies: Approved separate backup destination or existing backup facility
findings.cost_effect: Engineering and storage effort; recurring cost depends on the selected approved facility, outside the $50 AI/search ledger.

findings.problem: The GitHub Pages preview workflow can publish the wrong directory after a failed build and differs from the actual Sites Worker target.

evidence.detail: npm ci falls back to npm install; npm run build at line34 ignores failure. Directory selection sets dist then overwrites it with public at line46; public exists in this checkout.
Auxiliary workflow uses Node20 while main CI uses Node22 and hosting guidance supports Node22/24.
Canonical jobvance.io is a Cloudflare Worker through Sites, so this preview flaw is not evidence of a production v19 outage.

findings.recommendation: Retire the unused preview workflow or make it a clearly separate, fail-closed supported preview: npm ci, one supported runtime, successful build, explicit artifact path and route/security checks appropriate to that target.
acceptance_criteria: An intentionally failing build cannot upload or deploy an artifact.
Successful selection is explicit and cannot be overwritten by public/.
Workflow/docs name Sites as the canonical production route and state whether the Pages preview is supported.
dependencies: Decision on keeping the auxiliary preview
findings.cost_effect: No new hosting service required; may remove redundant deployments.

findings.problem: The generic operations guide gives invalid commands and a wrong hosting/health model, making recovery slower for a new maintainer.

evidence.detail: Guide references absent db:migrate; line61 uses type-check rather than package.json typecheck; line147 says Vercel/Netlify; line121 points at /health.
The available npm scripts do not implement the guide's database/e2e/format commands.
Read-only HEAD on14October2026 returned404; / and /check returned200 with no-cache and CSP. This is a stale instruction, not evidence that a promised production health service failed.

findings.recommendation: Replace the generic guide with a short index to current Sites and integrated-loop procedures; preserve historical notes as dated archives. Define the actual public route checks and private scheduler/budget checks operators should perform.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented command exists and is appropriate for a clean checkout.
A maintainer can identify production publisher, backend deployment ordering, pause controls and exact rollback receipt from one index.
Health guidance uses existing meaningful checks and distinguishes reachability from dependency progress.
findings.cost_effect: No recurring cost; reduces operator support/recovery time.

open_questions: Can the release owner supply a non-secret complete v19 receipt that maps backend source digests, schema migration-history hashes and active edge versions?
What backup facility currently exists outside the reviewed repository, who owns it, and when was the last successful isolated restore?
Are external alerts or branch protections configured outside the reviewed artifacts?
Is the testcodex Pages workflow still intentionally supported?
do_not_build_now: Kubernetes, Docker orchestration, multi-cloud failover or a new AWS/Vercel project for this ten-person pilot.
A paid observability platform before defining useful health signals and the operator response.
An uptime or RPO/RTO promise based only on code rollback or an untested backup.
